literal: Physical association and constant interaction are not necessary; shared feeling indeed will give the right of intimacy that is friendship.
translation: Constant physical association and long familiarity are not necessary for friendship; a shared feeling alone will yield the right of intimate friendship.
modern: நட்பு ஏற்படுவதற்கு உடலால் சேர்ந்து இருப்பதோ, பழகிக் கொண்டிருப்பதோ தேவையில்லை; மன உணர்வுகளின் ஒற்றுமை ஒன்றே நட்புக்குரிய உரிமையைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet explains that true friendship does not depend on physical proximity or long-term social interaction. The key words are 'புணர்ச்சி' (physical association) and 'பழகுதல்' (constant interaction), which are contrasted with 'உணர்ச்சி' (shared feeling or mental affinity). The poet asserts that 'உணர்ச்சி' alone is sufficient to create 'கிழமை', which means the right of intimacy or a deep bond of ownership between friends. Thus, true friendship is a union of minds rather than a mere habit of being together.
